themes_detail.label: Sudden Standing Water Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Standing water complaints spiked to 3 this week versus 0.2 weekly average over 8 weeks—a 1100% increase (z-score: 4.16)—suggesting a new drainage or flooding issue emerged in Tottenville/Great Kills this week that warrants immediate investigation.
evidence: 3 standing water complaints filed this week vs. 0.2 weekly baseline (1100% spike, z-score: 4.16)
Timing coincides with recent precipitation or potential infrastructure failure
Long-standing community board request for sewer infrastructure development suggests chronic vulnerability in specific street segments
reporting_angles: Interview residents in affected blocks to map extent and duration of standing water; determine if new construction or weather event triggered it
Cross-reference with DEP and NYC Parks records to identify which street segments lack sanitary sewers and are most vulnerable to pooling

themes_detail.label: Litter Basket Shortage Spike
themes_detail.summary: Litter basket requests jumped to 3 complaints this week versus 0.6 weekly average—a 380% increase (z-score: 3.41)—indicating residents in specific neighborhoods may be frustrated by inadequate waste receptacles.
evidence: 3 litter basket requests this week vs. 0.6 weekly average (380% spike, z-score: 3.41)
Aligns with recurring community board budget request for increased enforcement of illegal dumping laws
Suggests possible gap in public sanitation infrastructure or accumulation triggering resident complaints
reporting_angles: Identify which specific parks, waterfront areas, or street corridors are generating complaints and visit to assess actual trash conditions
Interview DSNY about basket placement criteria and whether Tottenville/Great Kills is underserved relative to other districts

themes_detail.label: Construction & Plumbing Surge
themes_detail.summary: General construction and plumbing complaints rose to 31 last week versus 15.4 weekly average—a 102% increase (z-score: 4.42)—coinciding with 741 DOB building permits filed over 90 days (375 alterations, 281 new buildings), suggesting active construction may be creating infrastructure strain or permit compliance issues.
evidence: 31 construction/plumbing complaints last week vs. 15.4 weekly baseline (102% spike, z-score: 4.42)
741 DOB permits filed in last 90 days, including 375 alterations and 281 new buildings, indicating active development intensity
Standing water spike and electrical complaints (up 233% two weeks ago) may indicate contractor-related infrastructure disruptions
reporting_angles: Map which 3-4 major construction projects (South Shore Industrial Center, Arden Heights Woods, 4450 Arthur Kill Road) are generating most complaints and interview residents adjacent to sites
Review DOB violation records to see if permit holders are violating working hours, traffic, or utility protection rules

themes_detail.label: Electrical Infrastructure Concerns
themes_detail.summary: Electrical complaints jumped to 10 two weeks ago versus 3.0 weekly average—a 233% increase (z-score: 3.4)—suggesting potential power outages, aging grid issues, or construction-related electrical damage in the district.
evidence: 10 electrical complaints two weeks ago vs. 3.0 weekly average (233% spike, z-score: 3.4)
Timing overlaps with construction/plumbing surge, suggesting potential contractor-caused electrical disruptions or utility conflicts
No recent Con Edison public notices or media reports identified, indicating potential underreporting or localized issue
reporting_angles: Contact Con Edison for outage logs and complaint records specific to Tottenville/Great Kills zip codes for past 2 weeks
Interview residents and businesses who filed complaints to determine if outages were brief or prolonged, and whether construction sites are near incidents

themes_detail.label: Tree Maintenance & Flooring Disruptions
themes_detail.summary: New tree requests spiked 1900% (5 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.2 baseline) and flooring/stairs complaints jumped 400% (5 complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 1.0 baseline)—both high z-scores—suggesting possible storm damage, infrastructure failures, or sidewalk/public space deterioration requiring investigation.
evidence: New tree requests: 5 complaints (2 weeks ago) vs. 0.2 weekly average (1900% spike, z-score: 10.97)
Flooring/stairs complaints: 5 (3 weeks ago) vs. 1.0 weekly average (400% spike, z-score: 4.62)
Long-standing community board request for forestry services and street tree maintenance indicates chronic underinvestment
reporting_angles: Interview Parks Department about tree planting/maintenance backlog; determine if recent weather or storm damaged trees or created safety hazards
Inspect reported flooring/stairs locations to assess trip/fall hazards, particularly on public stairs, transit stations, and pedestrian access points in waterfront or park areas
